title: Pullback is t-exact for the standard constructible t-structures
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\neq p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ contained in $\Qlb$, and let $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$, with the rationalized category $D^b_c(-,E)$ and the common-stage category $D^b_c(-,\Qlb)$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Let $h:W\to X$ be a morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let $Lh^*:D^b_c(X,\Lambda)\to D^b_c(W,\Lambda)$ be the derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Use on both sides the standard pair [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure], its constructible heart $\Sh_c(-,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-constructible-heart] and the cohomology functors $\mathcal H^j$ [prop-constructible-truncations].

Then $Lh^*$ is $t$-exact: $Lh^*D^{\le0}_c(X,\Lambda)\subset D^{\le0}_c(W,\Lambda)$ and $Lh^*D^{\ge0}_c(X,\Lambda)\subset D^{\ge0}_c(W,\Lambda)$. Consequently $Lh^*$ restricts to an exact functor $\Sh_c(X,\Lambda)\to\Sh_c(W,\Lambda)$, and for every $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and $j\in\mathbf Z$ the truncation maps induce a natural isomorphism $\mathcal H^j(Lh^*K)\cong Lh^*\mathcal H^j(K)$. In particular, for a geometric point $\bar x:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ [def-weil-geometric-point] and the point-fibre functor $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], $\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*\mathcal H^j(K))\cong\mathrm H^j(\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*K))$, and for $\mathcal F\in\Sh_c(X,\Lambda)$ the complex $\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*\mathcal F)$ is concentrated in degree zero. At $\Qlb$ all these maps are the scalar extensions of the corresponding maps at a common finite coefficient-field stage.

By [lem-a1-completed-perfect-scalar-pullback] its pullback has the same bound; the square in Step 1 identifies it with the output chart restriction. proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-texact-coefficient-stage-descent] to these integral pullbacks for all finite $E$. The integral bounded t-structures are [prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure]; coefficient transitions are exact by [lem-weil-scalar-extension-exact-triangulated], with the associators of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. The rational and common-stage halves are precisely the isomorphism closures in [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure]; [prop-constructible-truncations] supplies their bounded t-structures and scalar-compatible truncation maps. The comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] give the required identity and tower coherence; their termwise scalar maps commute with shifts on every reduction tower. The resulting functors are those of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Hence they are t-exact, exact on hearts, and have the stated canonical cohomology comparisons, commuting with finite coefficient extension.

proof.text: Apply Step 3 to $\bar x:s\to X$, also a morphism between finite-type $k$-schemes. Compose its cohomology comparison with [lem-a1-point-realization-standard-cohomology] to obtain $\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*\mathcal H^jK)\cong H^j(\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*K))$. A heart object pulls back to the point heart, whose realization is concentrated in degree zero by that lemma. Its scalar-cohomology squares together with Step 3 show that all these maps at $\Qlb$ are the scalar extensions of the maps at a common finite field.
